content:
alex.finance: Heads up 10: invoice INV-2026-0109 from Nimbus came in for $75,000. PDF shows $60k annual sub + $15k usage credits (expire 6mo). How should we treat the credits for revrec?

toni.revrec: Generally subscription recognized ratably. Usage credits are a liability (deferred) until consumed or expired. Need term dates & any roll-over clause.

sam.billing: Invoice posted to 4001 (SaaS Rev) for full $75k today. Oops. I'll need to reclass. Alex, can you confirm contract start and credit expiry?

alex.finance: Contract effective 2026-03-15. Credits valid until 2026-09-14, no roll-over. PO 7722.

toni.revrec: Ok: $60k subscription -> 12 month ratable starting 3/15 -> recognize pro rata for March; $15k credits -> defer to 2195 (Deferred Credits) and amortize to revenue only when consumed. If unused by 9/14, recognize breakage per policy (estimate) at 9/30.

sales-ops: FYI SF product mapping uses NIMBUS-ANNUAL only; billing didn't break out the credits as a separate line. We'll fix mapping. @sam.billing can we get the invoice line-level override?

sam.billing: I'll re-post as two lines. Plan: JE1 today (reclass): Dr 4001 15,000 Cr 2195 15,000. Add memo: "Reclass unearned credits INV-2026-0109."

toni.revrec: For March close: subscription revenue recognized = $60k * (17/365) = $2,794.52 (pro rata for 3/15-3/31). Book that monthly/periodic schedule.
alex.finance: Can you round and include in the close schedule? We need to show the prorata calc in the close pack.
toni.revrec: Will create revenue schedule in NetSuite: start 2026-03-15, monthly recognition, include one-off prorate entry for March. I'll attach calc.
sam.billing: Uploaded draft JE and invoice PDF to Close Checklist: https://drive.company/close/nimbus_INV-2026-0109 (internal link). Tagged @alex.finance.
audits-bot: Audit note added: "Deferred credits reclassification for Nimbus INV-2026-0109". Reviewer: Toni RevRec.
alex.finance: Any breakage estimate required now or wait until 9/30?
toni.revrec: We estimate breakage now using historical redemption rate (20%). For conservative policy we'll recognize 80% as liability and 20% as expected breakage to revenue at contract inception per ASC 606. So book 15k * 20% = 3,000 as immediate revenue? Wait: breakage should be recognized as revenue proportionally as other performance obligations are satisfied or when pattern can be reasonably estimated. Given short expiry, we can estimate now and book $3k of breakage to 4005 and $12k to 2195. Update: discuss with auditors if policy conservative.
audits-bot: Auditor flag: Please include breakage methodology and historical data in close pack for review.
sam.billing: I'll implement JE changes but will mark breakage as pending until Toni confirms.

alex.finance: Action items: Sam reclass + upload final JEs; Toni prepare schedule & breakage support; Sales-ops fix SF mapping. Closing loop by EOD tomorrow. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
